e.etymology: A spelling of Chad, from the Old English name Ceadda, borne by a 7th-century English bishop and saint. Its meaning is not known.

assoc.t: sounds the same as Chad, slang for a cocky alpha male

e.meaning: dimple, a small hollow in the cheek
e.etymology: The English word for a small hollow in the cheek, used as a girl's name in the American South around 1900. It is also a given name in India.
A variant of Alberta, the feminine of Albert, from Germanic words for noble and bright.
The German form of Gerard, from the Germanic words ger, spear, and hard, brave or hardy.
A 1960s American name that sets the sound of Tonya on the -da ending of Rhonda and Wanda.
A spelling of Glenda, a Welsh name of the 20th century made from glan, pure or holy, and da, good. The spelling also echoes Glinda of Oz.
A spelling of Linwood, an English place name and surname from Old English lind, the lime or linden tree, and wudu, wood.
A spelling of Phyllis, Greek for foliage. In Greek myth Phyllis died of love and was turned into an almond tree.
An American coinage of the 1980s that joins the prefix Sha- with the -quita of Marquita and Chiquita.
A spelling of Ethel, a short form of Old English names such as Etheldreda and Ethelinda, which begin with aethel, noble.

assoc.t: ethyl, a chemistry term, as in ethyl alcohol

e.note: Ethyl is a chemistry term (ethyl alcohol) and was a trade name for leaded gasoline additive.

e.etymology: A spelling of Felicia, the feminine of Felix, Latin for lucky or happy. The actress Phylicia Rashad made this spelling known in the 1980s as Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show.
namesakes: Phylicia Rashad (actress, Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show)

assoc.t: Phylicia Rashad, Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show

e.etymology: Merle with the -ene ending, part of a mid-century fashion for names like Darlene and Earlene.
A Scottish surname, a contraction of the Norman place name Normanville. John Home gave it to the hero of his 1756 play Douglas, which spread it as a first name.
A 1970s American form of Tasha, the short form of Natasha, said with the sound of Marsha.
From the Germanic words adal, noble, and beraht, bright. Albert is a shortened form of the same name.
A spelling of Galen, from Greek Galenos, calm, the name of the 2nd-century physician whose writings shaped medicine for centuries.
A phonetic spelling of Arthur from 19th-century American records. Arthur is a Celtic name often linked with a word for bear, though its source is not settled.
A spelling of Hilliard, an English surname from the medieval woman's name Hildiard, a Norman form of Hildegard.
A spelling of Sheena, the English form of Scottish Gaelic Sine, which is the Gaelic form of Jane or Jean.
An English place name and surname from Old English burh, fort, and leah, woodland clearing.
e.note: Sounds the same as burly, big and heavily built; burley is also a type of tobacco.

e.etymology: A blend of Glen or Glenda with Dora. Glendora, California, was named the same way in 1887, from glen and the founder's wife Leadora.
A spelling of Earline, a feminine form of Earl, the English title, from Old English eorl, nobleman.
From the Germanic words hild, battle, and gard, enclosure or protection. Saint Hildegard of Bingen, the 12th-century abbess and composer, is its best known bearer.
namesakes: Hildegard of Bingen (12th-century abbess, composer and saint)

e.etymology: An American coinage of the 1970s that puts the prefix La- before Trina, the short form of Katrina.
e.note: One letter away from latrine, a word for a toilet, which invites teasing.

e.etymology: A compound of George or Georgia with Ann. George comes from Greek georgos, farmer; Ann from Hebrew Hannah, grace.
An English place name and surname from Old English north and tun, a farm or settlement to the north.
A spelling of Brittany, the English name of the region in northwest France settled by Britons. It was a leading American girl's name around 1990.
A spelling of Kimberly, from an English place name meaning the woodland clearing of a woman named Cyneburg. It became a given name after the South African town of Kimberley.
An American coinage of the 1980s that puts the prefix La- before Kendra.
An American coinage of the 1980s that joins the prefix Sha- with the -quana ending heard in Laquana.
A spelling of Sheila, the English form of Irish Sile, which is the Irish form of Cecilia, a Roman family name.
A spelling of Lavern or Laverne, from a French place name and surname meaning the alder tree. Both men and women carried it in the early 20th century.
